newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean president's son in parliament for probe.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean president's son in parliament for probe.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam's controversial son appeared in parliament on Friday at the climax of a special probe into a loans-for-kickbacks scandal that has rocked the nation.

Lawmakers have said they will grill Kim Hyun-chul, 38, the second son of the beleaguered president, over allegations that he took a massive pay-off in a deal involving the failed Hanbo Steel Co at the centre of the scandal.

Kim Hyun-chul entered the National Assembly wearing a dark business suit and bowed deeply before taking his place behind a microphone on a bench in the chamber. The hearing is being broadcast live on television.

State prosecutors have been delving into allegations that Kim Hyun-chul took a 200 billion won ($224 million) kickback from a businessman acting as an agent for Hanbo. The businessman has denied the charges.
Opposition lawmakers have also accused the junior Kim of meddling in state affairs by influencing important appointments and policy decisions.

Kim Hyun-chul played an important role in his father's presidential election in 1992, and opposition lawmakers have said they will question him over whether he kept some of the money left over from the campaign.
